item.description: This is more about who will pay the cost of the president’s war on Iran and how it’s disrupting the global flow of oil than it is a history lesson about Alaska oil production. But stay with me as I run through the history to get to my point.

item.title: Opinion: Alaska’s maritime economy works because we invest in people, not just projects
item.description: Reid Williams, a second-generation fisherman from Cordova, grew up in a fishing family and began working as a teenager. After graduating in 2019, he leased a vessel and permit while working to build something of his own. With support from the state’s Commercial Fishing Loan Program, he was able to purchase his first boat and permit, a step toward long-term ownership that would have been impossible to achieve through traditional financing.

item.description: The outbreak, caused by a rare Ebola species, is thought to have caused 139 deaths so far.

item.title: EasyJet boss says summer flights won't be hit by jet fuel shortages
item.description: The airline has seen no problems with fuel, but says people are booking later because of uncertainty caused by the Iran war.

item.title: Nvidia's record result fails to impress investors
item.description: The chip giant reported more stellar results but its shares fell after-hours as investors wonder if it can keep up its pace of growth amid greater competition.

item.title: Even as anxieties grow under Trump, these swing voters aren't ready to back Democrats
item.description: Swing voters in North Carolina say they are frustrated with President Trump and the state of the economy, but aren't ready to abandon him or his party as the midterms inch closer.

item.title: Spencer Pratt is 'winning the internet,' but can he become mayor of Los Angeles?
item.description: Pratt, a former reality TV star, is flooding social media with edgy humor, AI slop and combative rhetoric as a way of grabbing attention and winning the vote of the very online. It's a strategy some political experts see as the future of online campaigning.

item.title: The Education Department is hiring — while it's being dismantled
item.description: The Federal Student Aid office lost half its staff last year as part of Trump administration downsizing. Now, it's hiring hundreds of new workers.

item.title: A guide to converting your lawn into a wildlife friendly garden
item.description: Turning your grass into a garden isn't as complicated as you think, but it will take time and effort. This step-by-step guide breaks down the process, from killing your lawn to picking plants to grow.

item.title: As floods get worse, Britain tries a new solution: beavers
item.description: About 400 years ago, beavers were hunted to extinction across Britain. Now they're being reintroduced as little climate warriors, as communities harness their dam-building skills to mitigate flooding.

item.title: Wes Streeting pledges wealth tax as part of leadership pitch
item.description: He proposes equalising capital gains tax with income tax, in a reform he estimates could raise £12bn a year.

item.title: Chris Mason: Reeves' summer savings drive won't stretch to energy bills
item.description: The chancellor is announcing measures aimed at easing the cost of living - but no help yet with energy bills.
